triage.triage_reason: IHR基準4項目すべてに該当し、WHO国際的懸念事項の公衆衛生上の緊急事態宣言、複数国への国際的拡大、高い死亡率、治療・ワクチン欠落、医療従事者感染を含む。スクリーニング基準も5項目全てに該当。
triage.notes: ブンディブギョエボラウイルスによる急速な感染拡大。DRC Ituri州およびウガンダでの発生。WHO国際的懸念事項の公衆衛生上の緊急事態として宣言。500以上の疑似症例、約130死亡（検査確認は約30例）。アメリカ人医師がドイツに移送、接触者もドイツとチェコへ。ウガンダでも2例の確認例。発生地域にはウガンダ、ドイツ、チェコが含まれていますが、サマリー上で実際の感染イベント発生国は対象国リスト内ではDRCのみであるため、verified_locationsに含める対象国はDRCのみとします。

article.articleHeadline: Prymula varuje před ebolou: Sledovat by se měli všichni, kdo se teď vracejí z Konga a Ugandy
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Prymula Warns About Ebola: Everyone Returning from Congo and Uganda Should Be Monitored.
article.articleSummary: Ebola monitoring is advised for people returning to the Czech Republic from the Democratic Republic of Congo or Uganda, according to epidemiologist and former health minister Roman Prymula. An American physician who was in contact with an Ebola patient is being airlifted from Uganda and will be taken to Bulovka Hospital in Prague, a center for infectious diseases, for isolation and care. The aim is to prevent further spread and to treat if infection develops. The incubation period can reach 21 days; during the initial asymptomatic phase the person is not infectious. Treatment is mainly supportive, with some experimental drugs. Nosocomial transmission remains a concern for healthcare workers without PPE. ECDC data indicate over 500 probable Congo cases and about 130 deaths as of Monday. Ebola spreads via direct contact with blood or body fluids; returnees should be monitored and contact-limited to detect symptoms within the incubation window.

triage.headline_ja: プリムラがエボラについて警告：コンゴおよびウガンダから戻ってくるすべての人を監視すべき
triage.triage_reason: IHR基準で4項目中3項目（深刻な公衆衛生影響、異常性、国際拡大リスク）に該当。エボラ出血熱の多国間発生報告であり、フルRRA対象。
triage.notes: 記事サマリーでDRCとウガンダのエボラ発生が主題。ウガンダは対象国リストに含まれないため verified_locations に除外。チェコ（プラハ）はエボラ患者を受け入れる受動的な対象地域であり、発生地域ではないため除外。DRCにおける500例以上の可能性患者と130例の死亡が報告されており、フルRRA実施の正当性が高い。

article.articleHeadline: A Kiwanja (Rutshuru), la crainte est réelle au regard de la propagation du virus Ebola
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: In Kiwanja (Rutshuru), fear is real as the Ebola virus spreads.
article.articleSummary: More than 100 Ebola virus disease deaths have been declared in Ituri Province, with numerous confirmed and suspected cases in the neighboring Nord-Kivu province of the Democratic Republic of the Congo. In Kiwanja, Rutshuru Territory, Nord-Kivu, residents express fear about the virus’s rapid spread, while stressing the need to protect themselves. A local resident warns of the disease’s high fatality rate and the seriousness of the threat. In Mabungo, residents organize to install hand-washing kits and promote sanitary practices, underscoring community involvement in the response. Key measures urged include frequent handwashing with clean water and soap, avoiding consumption of animals found dead from unknown causes, avoiding handshakes or hugs, and seeking care at the nearest health center for headaches, malaise, or other symptoms. This is the DRC’s 17th Ebola outbreak, as of May 20, 2026.

triage.headline_ja: キワンジャ（ルツシュル）ではエボラウイルスの拡散を考えると恐れは現実である
triage.triage_reason: IHR基準で4項目全て該当。エボラは極めて高い致死率を持つ広範な公衆衛生上の脅威であり、DRC内での拡大と国際的な拡大リスク、渡航・貿易制限のリスクがある。
triage.notes: 記事サマリーはDRC（特にイトゥリ州・ノルドキヴ州）でのエボラ感染を主題としており、これはDRCの17番目のアウトブレイクである。発生地域にフィリピンが含まれているが、記事サマリーではフィリピンへの言及がなく、Mabunga/Calabarzonの地理的座標がフィリピン領内を示しているが、この記事の主題はDRCのエボラ事例に限定されるため、verified_locationsはDRCのみとした。

article.articleHeadline: Revue de presse internationale - À la Une: la menace Ebola
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: International Press Review - On the Front Page: The Ebola Threat.
article.articleSummary: An Ebola outbreak in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo, centered in Ituri’s Bunia, where Dr. Barabak Kano, 40, heads the Bunia Center for Neuro-Psychopathology, describes a collapsing response: patients panic, there is no vaccine or treatment for the Bundibugyo strain, and blood samples must be flown to Kinshasa with slow turnaround. Isolation wards are exhausted; shortages of medicines, PPE, beds, and mattresses force nurses to burn used bedding. Kinshasa health authorities and humanitarian groups are mobilizing, but field presence is limited. An American physician, Peter Stafford, tested positive and was evacuated to Germany; his wife Rebekah, also a doctor, is confined in Congo after contracting infection from an obstetrics patient. The New York Times cites over 130 suspected deaths and 540 cases in DRC and Uganda; authorities warn the outbreak could last months. The epicenter is Ituri, with spillovers to North and South Kivu and into Uganda; no vaccine exists.

triage.headline_ja: 国際ニュース速報 - 一面トップ：エボラ脅威
triage.triage_reason: IHR基準4項目すべて該当。エボラ出血熱の多国間での集団感染、死亡・重症例多数、国際的感染拡大リスク高く、国際支援と医療体制の危機的状況が確認される。フルRRA進行必須。
triage.notes: 記事サマリーによるとウガンダへの流行拡大言及があるが、Bluedot APIの発生地域リストに含まれるUganda（226074）は対象国リストに未掲載のため verified_locations から除外。DRCが主要な発生地であり、ドイツ（医療疎開先）、ウガンダ（隣接国での発生）の記載はあるがサマリーの主題はDRC東部のエボラ流行。Bundibugyo株による130人超の死亡、540例超の確認例、医療体制の崩壊、ワクチン・治療薬の欠如、複数州への拡大と国際的感染例が報告されており、極めて高いリスク。

article.articleHeadline: El ébola avanza en el Congo y Uganda mientras la OMS aumenta la financiación de emergencia
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola is spreading in the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Uganda as the WHO increases emergency funding.
article.articleSummary: Ebola is spreading in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) and Uganda, with over 500 suspected cases and 130 suspected deaths reported by the DRC Ministry of Health; 30 confirmed cases in the DRC. Declared May 15 in Ituri, the outbreak has reached ten health zones in Ituri and expanded to North Kivu with confirmed cases in Butembo and Goma. Uganda has two imported cases. The World Health Organization is deploying 3.4 million USD in emergency funds, bringing total to 3.9 million, and has sent 12 tons of supplies from Kinshasa and Nairobi, including PPE. WHO is boosting surveillance, contact tracing, diagnostics, clinical care, and cross-border preparedness; partners like Alima and Médecins Sans Frontières are installing treatment centers. A WHO technical group is reviewing candidate vaccines and therapies; Tedros addressed the International Health Regulations Emergency Committee amid rising urban cases in Kampala, Bunia, and Goma. Ituri remains insecure with displacement over 100,000.

triage.headline_ja: エボラがコンゴとウガンダで拡大し、WHOが緊急資金を増額
triage.triage_reason: IHR基準4項目全て該当。エボラ出血熱は公衆衛生上の最高リスク疾患であり、複数国への越境拡大、死亡例の報告、国際的な渡航・貿易規制のリスクを伴う。
triage.notes: エボラ出血熱は国際保健危機の最高リスク病原体。記事にはDRC（イトゥリ州、北キブ州）とウガンダでの確定例および疑い例の報告がある。ケニアはナイロビを通じた物資供給拠点であり、発生地として確認されていないため verified_locations から除外。WHO の国際保健規則緊急委員会招集、複数機関による対応展開が確認されている。

article.articleHeadline: Nhiều nước châu Á tăng cường biện pháp phòng dịch Ebola năm 2026
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Many Asian countries ramp up Ebola prevention measures in 2026.
article.articleSummary: Following WHO's declaration of a global Ebola emergency, several Asian countries tighten border controls and boost readiness. As of May 2026, Asia reports no confirmed cases. The Ituri province outbreak in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo has over 540 suspected cases and dozens of deaths, prompting alert. Thailand, Indonesia, Vietnam, Singapore, Japan, South Korea, Hong Kong, and Mainland China are strengthening entry screening and isolation plans. Thailand will screen arrivals from the DR Congo, Uganda, and other high-risk zones and stock PPE. Indonesia strengthens airport controls; Singapore requires 21-day self-monitoring or border testing for travelers from affected regions. Korea requires health-status declarations for travelers from DR Congo, Uganda, and South Sudan; Hong Kong audits quarantine facilities on Lantau; Mainland China requires health declarations for at-risk passengers with fever or nausea. India expands testing via the National Institute of Virology, Pune; Nepal boosts border surveillance. Despite low risk, vigilance remains essential.

triage.headline_ja: 多くのアジア諸国が2026年のエボラ出血熱対策を強化
triage.triage_reason: IHR基準3項目該当（深刻な公衆衛生影響、国際的拡大リスク、渡航制限リスク）。WHO による全球的エボラ緊急宣言下での複数国の防止措置強化と、DRC Ituri での540例以上の患者発生により、シグナルとして認識される。
triage.notes: DRC Ituri での540例以上の患者報告に基づき、WHO が全球エボラ緊急を宣言。記事はアジア 9 ヶ国における国境検疫強化・入国スクリーニング・PPE 備蓄などの予防措置について報道しており、対象国内での確認症例はないが、国際的な警戒態勢が構築されていることを示す。地域検証では、実際の発生地は DRC（対象国）および複数のアジア諸国の防止措置に焦点。

article.articleHeadline: 中国驻乌干达使馆提醒在乌中国公民注意防范埃博拉疫情
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: The Chinese Embassy in Uganda reminds Chinese citizens in Uganda to take precautions against the Ebola outbreak.
article.articleSummary: Ebola virus disease (EVD) imported case detected in Uganda with one death; Ugandan authorities have postponed large events and strengthened outbreak prevention and response measures. On May 17, the World Health Organization designated the Ebola outbreaks in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (Kinshasa) and Uganda as a Public Health Emergency of International Concern (PHEIC). The Ugandan Ministry of Health has identified Kampala and Wakiso, among 22 districts, as high-risk areas. The Chinese Embassy in Uganda urges Chinese citizens to monitor local developments, maintain personal hygiene, avoid contact with high-risk animals and with those confirmed, suspected, or in close contact with cases, minimize unnecessary travel and inter-district movement, and avoid crowded venues. Seek prompt medical care if symptoms appear. Uganda emergency number: +256-112; Chinese MFA emergency hotlines: +86-101308; +86-10-65612308.

triage.headline_ja: 中国駐ウガンダ大使館、ウガンダ在住中国人にエボラ疫情対策を呼びかけ
triage.triage_reason: IHR基準で4項目全て該当（深刻な公衆衛生影響、異常/予想外、国際的拡大リスク、渡航制限リスク）、WHO PHEIC指定されたエボラウイルス病の拡大と複数国への波及が確認されている。
triage.notes: 記事サマリーはウガンダとDRCの両国でのエボラ発生と複数地域への波及を記述しているが、発生地域にUganda（GeoNames IDが対象国リストに含まれていない）が含まれているため、verified_locationsはDRCのみとした。DRC発生のエボラがウガンダに輸入され、WHO PHEICが指定されている重大な国際的感染症危機。

article.articleHeadline: "Καμπανάκι" ΠΟΥ για τον θανατηφόρο Έμπολα: "Εξαπλώνεται πολύ γρήγορα"  #StarGrNews
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: "Alarm bell" from WHO about the deadly Ebola: "It is spreading very quickly" #StarGrNews
article.articleSummary: Ebola virus disease is spreading rapidly in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), centered in Ituri Province with Bunia a key hub. The World Health Organization has declared a public health emergency as the outbreak crosses borders. About 136 deaths and roughly 543 suspected cases are linked to Ebola, with few laboratory-confirmed samples. The Bundibugyo strain has no approved vaccine or therapy; containment relies on rapid detection, contact tracing, and infection-control measures. Authorities report intensified border checks, but the virus has crossed into Uganda, where one death and one case have been recorded, with no sustained local transmission yet. MSF reports overwhelmed facilities in Bunia. In Europe, an American physician infected in DRC is en route to Germany for treatment (Berlin’s Charité). The United States warns citizens against travel to DRC, South Sudan, Uganda, and Bahrain and will impose a one-month entry ban for travelers from these countries.

triage.headline_ja: WHO が致命的なエボラについて「警告信号」：「非常に急速に拡散している」
triage.triage_reason: IHR基準4項目すべてに該当。エボラ出血熱は公衆衛生上極めて重大で、DRC東部で急速に拡大し、ウガンダへの国境越え確認、国際的な症例移送により国際的拡大リスク顕著。WHOが公衆衛生上の緊急事態宣言、複数国による渡航制限措置実施中。
triage.notes: 記事サマリーでは DRC（Ituri Province, Bunia）を中心とした発生が記述されており、これが主題である。ウガンダでの1死亡・1症例報告も記載されているが、対象国リストにウガンダは含まれていないため verified_locations には含めない。ドイツ、アメリカ、スーダン、バーレーンは症例移送先または渡航制限実施国であり、発生地ではないため除外。Bundibugyo 株、ワクチン・治療法なし、境界を越えた感染確認、WHOの公衆衛生上の緊急事態宣言、複数国の渡航制限措置などから極めて高い優先度の案件。

article.articleHeadline: 민주콩고서 무섭게 퍼지는 에볼라···"내전에 미국 지원 삭감까지 겹친 대재앙"
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola Spreading Rapidly in the Democratic Republic of the Congo... A Catastrophe Compounded by U.S. Aid Cuts Amid the Civil War
article.articleSummary: Outbreak of Ebola in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, centered in North Kivu near Goma, with tests conducted at the National Biomedical Research Institute in Goma. WHO warns the outbreak’s scale and speed are concerning, potentially the third-largest on record. Ongoing conflict with M23 rebels and chronic underfunding have hampered early detection and response, surveillance, and supply stockpiles. As of May 20, 2026, Ebola suspected cases total 536, with 105 estimated, 34 laboratory-confirmed, and 134 deaths; officials warn that additional cases are likely. One American healthcare worker caring for patients was diagnosed May 17 and transferred to Germany. US aid cuts—USAID closure and HHS funding reductions from about 33 million USD in 2024 to under 10 million USD in 2025—are cited as weakening response capacity; The Lancet warned such cuts could yield more than 14 million deaths by 2030 if sustained.

triage.headline_ja: 民主コンゴで猛烈に広がるエボラ...「内戦に米国支援削減まで重なった大惨事」
triage.triage_reason: IHR基準4つすべてに該当し、WPRO基準5つすべてに該当。エボラウイルス病の大規模流行であり、国際的拡大リスク（米国職員感染、ドイツへの転送）と深刻な公衆衛生影響が確認された。
triage.notes: 記事サマリーに米国職員のドイツへの転送が記載されているが、エボラの実際の発生地はDRCであり、米国・ドイツは二次的な国際影響である。USAID削減による対応能力の低下が強調されており、社会政治的関心は極めて高い。推定死亡者134名、実験室確認症例34名、疑い症例536名という規模の大きさも懸念材料。

article.articleHeadline: Sécurité sanitaire : comment la Nouvelle-Calédonie se protège des maladies venues de l'extérieur ?
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Public health: how does New Caledonia protect itself from diseases coming from outside?
article.articleSummary: New Caledonia conducts border health surveillance at Tontouta International Airport, where travelers complete health declarations; each passenger is responsible, forming a prevention chain. The territory maintains PPE stockpiles (gloves, masks, gowns) in multiple sites, a COVID-19 lesson reinforced after riots. Forms collected by SIVAP are read and analyzed by DASS in Nouméa; the process is manual, twice weekly, focusing on travelers from South America and Africa, per WHO origin lists. A second phase cross-checks declared symptoms with destinations to flag potential carriers. If uncertainty remains, a DASS nurse intervenes: travelers from risk countries including Indonesia, Africa, and South America who declare non-vaccination against yellow fever or show symptoms are contacted and advised to seek medical attention; doctors should consider malaria, dengue, or measles, not only influenza. Malaria, dengue, measles, and yellow fever pose greater local risks than hantavirus or Ebola, under International Health Regulations for surveillance and anticipation.

triage.headline_ja: 公衆衛生：ニューカレドニアは外部からもたらされた病気からどのように身を守るか？
triage.triage_reason: 複数の感染症が言及されており、国際的な監視体制が描かれているが、具体的な発生事例や患者数が記述されておらず、実際のアウトブレイク・クラスターの報告ではなく公衆衛生体制の説明的記事である。情報が不足しているため経過観察が適切。
triage.notes: 記事はニューカレドニア（フランス領、対象国外）の国境衛生監視体制に関する説明的な内容。実際の患者発生やアウトブレイクの報告ではなく、インドネシア、アフリカ、南米からの旅行者監視の対象国としてのみ言及されている。具体的な疾患発生事例がないため、シグナルとしては識別困難であるが、複数感染症への言及と国際的な監視体制の存在から WATCH に分類。

article.articleHeadline: Il paziente zero, i primi test e i centinaia di casi sospetti: così è esplosa l'epidemia di Ebola Periodico Daily
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Patient Zero, the first tests and hundreds of suspected cases: this is how the Ebola epidemic exploded Periodico Daily
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) caused by Bundibugyo virus is expanding from Ituri province, with 30 laboratory-confirmed cases and more than 500 suspected cases across 10 health zones; the outbreak has reached North Kivu (Butembo and Goma) and has produced two imported cases in Uganda (one death). As of May 20, 2026, authorities report about 130 suspected deaths and 30 confirmed cases in the DRC. The index is not yet established; a May 5 death in Bunia, followed by funeral practices, is being investigated as a possible amplifier. Local Bunia tests were negative for the Zaire Ebola strain, with Kinshasa laboratories later confirming Bundibugyo. No licensed vaccine or therapy exists for Bundibugyo; Ervebo (Zaire strain) is being considered, but availability is projected in around two months, likely not sufficient to end the outbreak. Community engagement and safe burial practices are emphasized for containment.

triage.headline_ja: 患者ゼロ、最初の検査と数百の疑わしい症例：エボラ出血熱の流行はこのようにして爆発した
triage.triage_reason: IHR基準4つすべてに該当。エボラ出血熱の大規模流行で深刻な公衆衛生影響、予想外の拡大（Bundibugyo株の確認）、国際的拡大リスク（ウガンダへの輸入例・死亡例あり）、渡航制限のリスク有。WPRO基準も5つすべて該当。フルリスク評価が必要。
triage.notes: Bundibugyo株によるエボラ出血熱流行。確認症例30例、疑い症例500例以上、死亡報告約130例。Ituri州から始まり北キブ州（ブテンボ、ゴマ）に拡大。ウガンダへの輸入例あり（死亡1例）。治療法やBundibugyo対応ワクチンの利用可能性が課題。2026年5月20日現在。

article.articleHeadline: Шефът на СЗО предупреди: Разпространението на ебола буди "сериозно безпокойство"
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: The WHO chief warned: The spread of Ebola raises "serious concern".
article.articleSummary: WHO Director-General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus warned that the Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) and Uganda raises serious concern. Over 130 deaths are likely linked, with more than 500 suspected cases. The WHO declared a Public Health Emergency of International Concern (PHEIC) on Saturday. Cases have appeared in urban areas such as Kampala, Goma, and Bunia. Nosocomial transmission has been observed, with healthcare workers among the deceased. Security in Ituri Province has deteriorated since May, driving displacement of over 100,000 people in two months and heightening spread as movement increases. Bundibugyo Ebola virus strain, for which there are no vaccines or specific treatments, drives the outbreak. Transmission occurs via direct contact with bodily fluids, contaminated objects, or deceased patients; symptoms include fever, fatigue, muscle pain, headache, vomiting, diarrhea, abdominal pain, and kidney/liver dysfunction. The U.S. has dispatched disaster response teams to DRC and Uganda.

triage.headline_ja: WHO事務局長の警告：エボラの拡大は「深刻な懸念」を引き起こしている
triage.triage_reason: エボラ出血熱の確定的なアウトブレイク（130人以上の死亡、500人以上の疑い例）であり、IHR基準4項目すべてに該当。WHO は PHEIC（国際的に懸念される公衆衛生上の緊急事態）を宣言済み。
triage.notes: 記事サマリーはウガンダでの症例出現を述べているが、ウガンダは対象国リストに含まれていないため verified_locations には含めない。DRC が主要な発生地であり、国際的な懸念事項として WHO から PHEIC 宣言が出ている。医療施設での伝播（ノゾコミアル感染）、都市部への拡大、セキュリティ悪化に伴う人口移動による拡大リスクが確認されている。

article.articleHeadline: "Ο Έμπολα μας έχει βασανίσει": Ο φόβος κυριαρχεί στο Κονγκό καθώς ο φονικός ιός εξαπλώνεται | LiFO
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: "Ebola has plagued us": Fear dominates in the Democratic Republic of the Congo as the deadly virus spreads | LiFO
article.articleSummary: Ebola virus disease caused by Bundibugyo ebolavirus is driving fear in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo, with Ituri province as epicenter. By May 20, 2026, authorities reported 514 suspected cases and 136 probable deaths, with one death in neighboring Uganda. Cases have been detected in Butembo and Goma in North Kivu, and in South Kivu. The outbreak traces to a nurse in Bunia who died in Mongbalu; she is considered the likely index case, with alerts only from May 8 and first official confirmation on April 24. Bundibugyo is less common in DRC, with previous outbreaks in 2007 and 2012 and a ~30% fatality rate. Symptoms may be subtler than other strains, delaying diagnosis and allowing silent spread. Public mistrust and misattribution to malaria or curses complicate response; displacement and conflict heighten challenges, with Save the Children warning of a crisis and risk to Goma, a hub under M23 control.

triage.headline_ja: 「エボラは私たちを苦しめてきた」：民主共和国コンゴで恐怖が支配、致命的なウイルスが拡大 | LiFO
triage.triage_reason: IHR基準3つ以上該当（深刻な公衆衛生影響、予想外の病原体・地域、国際的拡大リスク）、WPRO基準5つ全て該当。エボラウイルス感染症の確認された多地域流行であり、死亡例、ウガンダへの国境越え例、紛争地域での管理課題がある。
triage.notes: Bundibugyo ebolavirus（ブンディブギョ型）による流行は稀。514疑い症例・136確定/推定死亡例、ウガンダでの1死亡例により国際的拡大の証拠あり。紛争地域（M23支配下のゴマ）での管理課題、公衆衛生システムの脆弱性、疾病誤認識による対応遅延が懸念される。ウガンダへの越境例が記録されているが、ウガンダ内での患者検出状況の詳細は記事に示されていないため、DRCのみを verified_locations とした。

article.articleHeadline: Ο ΠΟΥ κρούει τον κώδωνα για τον Έμπολα: "Η επιδημία δεν θα τελειώσει σε δύο μήνες"
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: The WHO sounds the alarm on Ebola: "The outbreak will not end in two months"
article.articleSummary: Ebola Virus Disease outbreak in Ituri, DRC, driven by Bundibugyo strain, persists amid conflict. Ituri remains the epicenter, with severe shortages of medical supplies as fighting hampers aid delivery. Doctors Without Borders reports overwhelmed hospitals unable to admit new suspected cases. Authorities say about 136 deaths and over 540 suspected cases have been recorded, though laboratory confirmation is limited and totals may be higher due to underreporting and delays. Ebola transmits via contact with infected bodily fluids and causes severe hemorrhagic fever with high mortality; there is no approved vaccine or specific therapy for Bundibugyo. Containment relies on rapid case finding, isolation, and hygiene. WHO cautions the outbreak will not end in two months; past outbreaks have lasted years, and trajectory depends on response speed and scale. Additional cases in South Kivu and a case in Goma; patients and contacts evacuated to Europe for monitoring and quarantine.

triage.headline_ja: WHO、エボラ熱に警告を鳴らす：「この流行は2ヶ月では終わらない」
triage.triage_reason: IHR基準4つすべてに該当。Bundibugyo株によるエボラ出血熱の継続的な流行で、高い死亡率、紛争による対応困難、国際的な患者搬出、WHO警告による国際的関心が確認される。
triage.notes: Bundibugyo株によるエボラ出血熱は稀な株。紛争により医療支援の提供が著しく困難。136人の死亡と540人以上の疑い例が報告されているが、検査室確認が限定的で実数はより高い可能性。患者・濃厚接触者がヨーロッパへ搬出されており、国際的な伝播リスクが顕在化している。WHO声明により高い国際的関心あり。

article.articleHeadline: Zambia Activates Ebola Response Centres Following DRC Outbreak - Muvi TV
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in neighboring Democratic Republic of the Congo triggers Zambia to activate full health screening at all border entry points as of 2026-05-20. The World Health Organization (WHO) and the Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention (Africa CDC) have declared the DRC Ebola outbreak a Public Health Emergency of International Concern (PHEIC) and a continental concern. Zambia’s response focuses on detecting potential cases and preventing cross-border transmission through comprehensive border screening; the excerpt provides no case or death counts, laboratory confirmation details, or identified infection sources. The PHEIC designation underscores heightened international and regional attention and may prompt intensified cross-border surveillance and public health measures to mitigate spread between DRC and Zambia.

triage.headline_ja: ザンビア、DRC集団発生を受けてエボラ対応センターを発動
triage.triage_reason: IHR基準3項目該当（深刻な公衆衛生影響、国際的拡大リスク、渡航制限リスク）。WHOによりPHEIC指定済みのエボラ集団発生に対する国境対応活動。
triage.notes: WHOおよびAfrica CDCによるPHEIC指定済み。DRCでの集団発生に対するザンビアの国境対応（全国境検問所での健康スクリーニング）が報じられている。具体的な患者数や死亡者数は記事サマリーでは未報告。

article.articleHeadline: Appels sur l'actualité - VOS QUESTIONS - Spéciale Ebola
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Current Events Call-Ins - YOUR QUESTIONS - Ebola Special
article.articleSummary: As of May 20, 2026, the Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo has been declared a Public Health Emergency of International Concern (PHEIC). The event is linked to a viral variant for which there is neither a vaccine nor a treatment. The article describes a French-language radio segment, Current Events Call-Ins - Ebola Special, that invites listener input on the medical response, transmission modes, and public awareness. No case counts, symptoms, laboratory confirmation, or transmission chains are provided in the text. The piece underscores ongoing international concern and the lack of targeted countermeasures for this variant, while soliciting public commentary on response effectiveness and information dissemination. No additional epidemiological details are included within the article.

triage.headline_ja: 時事通信 - あなたの質問 - エボラ特集
triage.triage_reason: エボラウイルス病のPHEIC宣言により、IHR基準（深刻な公衆衛生影響、予想外性、国際拡大リスク、渡航・貿易制限リスク）の全4基準に該当する可能性が高く、WPROスクリーニング基準も複数該当。国際的な関心が極めて高い。
triage.notes: PHEIC宣言済みのエボラアウトブレーク。ワクチンおよび治療法がない新規ウイルス変異体が関連している。記事は具体的な症例数、確認例、感染チェーンの詳細を提供していないが、公式な国際的警告レベルの宣言と国際的懸念が明示されている。フルRRA進行が必須。

article.articleHeadline: 外交部：目前暂无中国公民疑似感染埃博拉病例
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ministry of Foreign Affairs: There are currently no suspected Ebola infection cases among Chinese citizens.
article.articleSummary: May 20, 2026 — The Chinese Foreign Ministry reports no suspected Ebola infections among Chinese citizens. Spokesperson Guo Jiakun notes ongoing Ebola outbreaks in the Central Africa region, specifically the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Uganda. China will maintain close communication with affected governments and, with the international community, provide all possible assistance to help quell the outbreak. The ministry has issued public announcements and Chinese embassies have issued consular reminders; Chinese nationals abroad are advised to strengthen precautions. China emphasizes its long-standing friendship with Africa (over 70 years) and solidarity in fighting Ebola and other diseases, pledging to respond with measures within its capability as the situation evolves. No cases among Chinese citizens have been confirmed or are suspected at this time.

triage.headline_ja: 外交部：目前暂无中国公民疑似感染埃博拉病例
triage.triage_reason: エボラ出血熱の発生がDRC及びウガンダで確認されており、IHR基準3項目（深刻な公衆衛生影響、異常性、国際的拡大リスク）が該当。シグナルとして識別される。
triage.notes: 記事サマリーでDRC及びウガンダでのエボラ発生が明記されている。中国での患者報告はない（外交部声明）。ウガンダは対象国リストに未含まれため verified_locations には DRC のみ記載。エボラ出血熱は複数の深刻度・流行性基準に該当し、国際的関心も高い。

article.articleHeadline: Groźny wirus coraz bliżej Polski?
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: A dangerous virus getting closer to Poland?
article.articleSummary: An American physician with suspected Ebola exposure is being transported to Prague for specialized care. The patient, who has no symptoms, reportedly contacted the Ebola virus in Uganda and will be admitted to the Bulovka University Hospital in a dedicated isolation cabin with clearly defined safety and outbreak-control measures. He is expected to remain under observation for three weeks. Bulovka is among facilities equipped to treat highly dangerous infectious diseases, featuring isolated rooms and a negative-pressure ward. World agencies had previously flagged six at-risk individuals bound for European hospitals, including one destined for Prague. The Ebola outbreak has activity in northeastern Democratic Republic of Congo since April, with two confirmed cases in Uganda. The World Health Organization has declared the outbreak a public health emergency of international concern; there is no vaccine or proven treatment for this variant.

triage.headline_ja: 危険なウイルスがポーランドに近づいている？
triage.triage_reason: IHR基準3項目該当（重度公衆衛生影響・異常性・国際拡大リスク）、WHO緊急事態宣言済み、エボラウイルス疑い患者のプラハ搬送という国際的な事象。
triage.notes: Bluedot APIが付与した発生地域にはPrague、Czechia、Polandが含まれているが、記事サマリーでは患者接触地がUgandaで、搬送先がPragueである。実際のエボラ発生地はDRCおよびUgandaであり、Chechiaへの患者搬送は対象国リストに含まれていないため、verified_locationsはDRCのみ。ただしUganda（対象国外）での確定症例2例も記事に明記されている。WHO緊急事態宣言済みであり、患者の国際搬送によりWPRO基準全項目該当。高度なシグナルとして判定。

article.articleHeadline: La OMS envía 12 toneladas de suministros de emergencia para frenar el avance del ébola en la RDC | Noticias ONU
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: WHO sends 12 tonnes of emergency supplies to curb the Ebola outbreak in the DRC | UN News
article.articleSummary: May 20, 2026 update: the World Health Organization dispatched 12 tonnes of emergency supplies and deployed 35 experts and responders to curb the Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo. The outbreak now has more than 500 suspected cases and 130 deaths and has extended to Ituri and North Kivu provinces, with cases also detected in Uganda. The identified strain is Bundibugyo ebolavirus, for which there are no approved vaccines or treatments currently available; vaccination would take at least two months before any immunization could begin. The response prioritizes rapid logistics, field expertise, and cross-border containment amid ongoing transmission risk. The article underscores the international health effort to slow the outbreak and the absence of immediately deployable medical countermeasures against Bundibugyo Ebola virus.

triage.headline_ja: WHO sends 12 tonnes of emergency supplies to curb the Ebola outbreak in the DRC | UN News
triage.triage_reason: IHR基準4項目すべてに該当。Bundibugyo ebolavirus による500以上の疑い例と130名の死亡を伴うエボラ出血熱の多国家発生であり、国際的拡大リスク、重篤な公衆衛生影響、渡航・貿易制限リスクが全て認められる。
triage.notes: 記事サマリーでウガンダでの症例検出が記載されているが、Bluedot APIの発生地域にはウガンダが含まれていても、本レポートの主要な焦点はDRCである。DRC内のIturi州とNorth Kivu州での発生が中心。ウガンダは対象国リストに含まれていないため、verified_locations にはDRCのみ含める。Bundibugyo ebolavirus は自然界での人畜共通感染症として知られており、ワクチン・治療法の欠如が対応の課題となっている。

article.articleHeadline: Πιο συχνές και πιο επικίνδυνες οι επιδημίες | Η ΚΑΘΗΜΕΡΙΝΗ
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: More frequent and more dangerous epidemics | Kathimerini
article.articleSummary: Recent hantavirus cases aboard the cruise ship MV Hindus triggered an international health alert, though the outbreak was quickly controlled. A Global Preparedness Monitoring Board (GPMB) report warns that infections from pathogens such as hantavirus and Ebola are increasing in frequency and potential severity, with pandemic risk levels surpassing current preparedness. Amid a fresh Ebola surge in Uganda and the Democratic Republic of the Congo, the WHO Director-General declared an emergency. Reuters reports that the Ebola crisis drained PPE stocks in Kinshasa, the DRC’s capital. Experts attribute rising infectious disease activity to climate change and ongoing global conflicts, while geopolitical fragmentation and competing commercial interests undermine coordinated response and preparedness. Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus also noted that this is not a crisis in isolation, highlighting funding cuts to global health programs as a contributing factor.

triage.headline_ja: より頻繁でより危険になる流行病 | カティメリニ
triage.triage_reason: IHR基準4項目すべてに該当（公衆衛生への深刻な影響、異常性、国際的拡大リスク、渡航制限リスク）。エボラとハンタウイルスの同時多発的な流行警告、WHO事務局長による緊急事態宣言、複数国での感染確認により、シグナルとして識別される。
triage.notes: 記事サマリーはエボラウイルスとハンタウイルスの複合的な脅威を扱い、DRC（キンシャサ）でのエボラ急増とウガンダでの感染拡大を明記。ウガンダは対象国リストに含まれていないため verified_locations には含めない。WHO事務局長による緊急事態宣言、複数国での同時流行、GPMB報告による警告により、公衆衛生上の深刻な懸念が確認された。

article.articleHeadline: FAAN promises enhanced Ebola preparedness at airports
article.articleSummary: FAAN announces enhanced Ebola preparedness at Nigeria's international airports amid the Bundibugyo ebolavirus outbreak in Central Africa. Working with Port Health Services and the Nigeria Centre for Disease Control, FAAN intensified surveillance of arrivals, especially from high-risk regions. Passengers are screened for Ebola symptoms; suspected cases will be isolated and undergo secondary health checks per national and international protocols. Coordination with stakeholders, staff training, and emergency response procedures have been strengthened to ensure swift action. No confirmed Ebola case has been reported in Nigeria. This follows the World Health Organization’s May 17, 2026 designation of the outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Uganda as a Public Health Emergency of International Concern. The outbreak is centered in DRC’s Ituri Province with spread to Uganda, raising regional concern due to reported cases and deaths. Passengers are urged to comply with screening and report symptoms.

triage.headline_ja: FAAN、空港でのエボラ対応強化を約束
triage.triage_reason: IHR基準3つ該当（深刻な公衆衛生影響、国際的拡大リスク、渡航制限リスク）。WHO公式にPHEIC指定済みの中央アフリカエボラ流行に対するナイジェリア国内対応報道。対象国DRCおよびウガンダでの確認事例あり。
triage.notes: Bundibugyo ebolavirus（BDBV）はエボラウイルスの亜種。DRC Ituri州での発生が主要な事象。ウガンダへの拡大も記事で言及されているが、ウガンダは対象国リストに含まれていないため除外。ナイジェリアは航空港での準備対応が主要トピックだが、確認事例なし。WHOが2026年5月17日にPHEIC指定した重要な流行イベント。

article.articleHeadline: Ebola in der Demokratischen Republik Kongo: Geld- und Sicherheitslage bremsen die Reaktion
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola in the Democratic Republic of the Congo: Funding and Security Situation Slow the Response.
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo is hampered by funding cuts and ongoing conflict, delaying testing and deployment of response teams. WHO warns that high positivity rates and growing clusters imply a much larger true scale than reported. Field delays in processing samples and restricted access to affected areas reduce detection, risking multi-generation transmission. The circulating Ebola variant is described as particularly unpredictable, with potentially higher case fatality. A severe shortage of vaccines and effective therapies means non-pharmaceutical measures must bear the burden: rapid testing, safe isolation, stringent contact tracing, and rigorous infection prevention in clinics and communities. Funding competition and logistical bottlenecks for diagnostics, cold-chain logistics, and mobile laboratories complicate the response. Emphasis on epidemiological surveillance, lab confirmation, field teams, clear community communication, data governance, and prioritized regional responses is needed.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ民主共和国のエボラ：資金および安全保障状況が対応を遅延させている
triage.triage_reason: IHR基準4つすべて該当。エボラウイルスは深刻な公衆衛生影響、高い死亡率、国際拡大リスク、渡航制限リスクをもたらす。現在の対応不十分状況はシグナルとしてのリスクを高める。
triage.notes: エボラ outbreak は継続中で、資金不足・セキュリティ状況による対応遅延が明記されている。WHOは報告数より実際の感染規模が大きいと警告。多世代感染リスク、ワクチン不足、診断遅延が指摘されており、国際的な支援と詳細なRRAが必須。

article.articleHeadline: Ebola'ya Yakalanan ABD Vatandaşı Almanya'da Tedavi Görecek
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola-infected American citizen will be treated in Germany.
article.articleSummary: An Ebola-infected American citizen will be treated in Berlin at Charité University Hospital, after being evacuated from the Democratic Republic of the Congo, where the latest outbreak is ongoing. The transfer to Germany was requested by the United States, citing Germany’s specialized facilities and closer proximity to the outbreak zone. German authorities say there is no risk to the general public. Six high-risk contacts who had contact with the patient will be brought to Germany for observation. Germany’s Development Minister Reem Alabali-Radovan called the Africa outbreak extremely serious and said 500 protective suits will be sent to the region next week to bolster response.

triage.headline_ja: エボラウイルスに感染したアメリカ国民がドイツで治療を受ける
triage.triage_reason: IHR基準3つ以上該当（深刻な公衆衛生への影響、国際的な拡大リスク、渡航制限のリスク）。エボラウイルスによる進行中のアウトブレイク、複数国への患者移送、国際支援の需要など複数のシグナルを満たす。
triage.notes: 記事サマリーはコンゴ民主共和国でのエボラアウトブレイクが主題。患者がドイツに移送されているが、実際の発生地はDRCのみ。Bluedot APIが付与したベルリン・ドイツは「治療地」であり発生地ではないため、verified_locationsから除外。アメリカは移送元国だが、対象国リストに含まれていないため除外。

article.articleHeadline: Escalada do ebola deixa OMS em alerta
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola escalation puts WHO on alert.
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) escalates, with 136 deaths and 543 suspected cases reported, as of mid-May 2026. Laboratory confirmation remains limited; the outbreak is caused by the Bundibugyo strain, for which there is no specific vaccine or therapy, though the WHO is evaluating candidate vaccines or treatments. Transmission is driven mainly by close contact with the secretions of infected individuals, spreading rapidly in precarious settings with scarce health services, few isolation areas, and inadequate bed distancing. The epicenter is Ituri Province in northeastern DRC, near Uganda and South Sudan, a gold-mining region with high population movement. Suspected cases have emerged in Butembo (North Kivu) and Goma, the latter under influence of the M23 group. Western actors warn of broader risk: the U.S. maintains a Level 4 travel advisory for DRC, South Sudan, and Uganda; Rwanda is advised to reconsider travel, while CDC says U.S. risk remains low. The U.S. plans to open about 50 clinics in the DRC and has provided substantial aid (≈R$65.4 million). Containment focuses on rapid case detection, isolation, and PPE provision.

triage.headline_ja: エボラの拡大、WHO警戒態勢へ
triage.triage_reason: IHR基準4項目すべてに該当し、エボラウイルス病（Bundibugyo株）の多発死亡例（136名）・国際的拡大リスク・渡航制限実施という重大な感染症危機である。
triage.notes: 2026年5月時点でのエボラ（Bundibugyo株）の大規模アウトブレイク。DRC東北部Ituri州が震源地で、ウガンダ・南スーダン国境地域という地政学的リスク高地。限定的な実験室確認、ワクチン不在、不十分な感染制御基盤が懸念。米国による大規模支援（約R$65.4百万）・渡航勧告（Level 4）発出など、国際的対応が活発化している。

article.articleHeadline: U.S. funds establishment of 50 Ebola response clinics in DRC, Uganda
article.articleSummary: The United States will rapidly fund up to 50 Ebola treatment clinics in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) and Uganda to establish clinical care and containment perimeters around affected areas. Clinics will provide emergency Ebola screening, triage, and isolation capacity, accelerating frontline medical care, critical humanitarian assistance, and outbreak response capabilities in communities at greatest risk. Funding will expand emergency treatment capacity, strengthen field operations, and speed delivery of protective equipment and diagnostics, while ensuring essential health services remain accessible. The announcement emphasizes a rapid, resourced, cooperative response with key global health partners, to prevent further spread of the outbreak. Funding will be delivered primarily via UN CERF pooled funding vehicles administered by OCHA, building on a 2025 funding tranche and a strengthened partnership to deliver aid faster and more efficiently.

triage.headline_ja: 米国がDRCとウガンダのエボラ対応クリニック50施設の設立に資金提供
triage.triage_reason: エボラ出血熱は異常性・予想外性が高く、国際的拡大リスク、深刻な公衆衛生への影響が存在。IHR基準2つ以上該当し、国際支援が既に動員されている。
triage.notes: Ugandaは対象国リストに含まれていないため verified_locations から除外。記事サマリーではDRCとウガンダ両国での対応クリニック設立が言及されているが、DRCのみが対象国。エボラ出血熱の流行・拡大リスクは高く、既に米国を含む国際的支援体制が構築されている段階。フルRRA実施推奨。

article.articleHeadline: इबोला के लक्षण क्या हैं और इससे बचाव कैसे हो सकता है? - BBC News हिंदी
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: What are the symptoms of Ebola and how can it be prevented?
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo has resulted in at least 100 deaths and hundreds of infections, according to the Africa Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (Africa CDC) chief cited by BBC. The report highlights ongoing transmission within the DRC and poses questions about the outbreak’s origins, asking where the first Ebola case was recorded and what its symptoms are. The piece centers on public health concerns regarding symptom recognition and early detection to curb spread, without detailing specific clinical features or laboratory confirmation in the excerpt. Dated 2026-05-20, the article foregrounds the need for rapid identification of initial cases and effective prevention measures in the affected region.

triage.headline_ja: エボラウイルスの症状は何か、そしてそれからどのように身を守ることができるか？
triage.triage_reason: IHR基準で4項目すべてに該当（重大な公衆衛生影響、深刻度と異常性、国際拡大リスク、渡航制限リスク）。WPRO基準でも全5項目該当。エボラアウトブレイクは最高レベルの懸念事項として認識される。
triage.notes: エボラウイルス病（Ebola Virus Disease）はIHR(2005)で最も重大な感染症のひとつ。現在の報告では少なくとも100人の死亡と数百の感染が確認されており、DRC国内での継続的な伝播が続いている。この記事はBBC Hindiが公開した啓発記事であり、症状認識と早期検出の重要性を強調している。国際的な支援と WHO への通知が必須の状況。

article.articleHeadline: Reprezentanca DR Konga bo lahko potovala v ZDA kljub izbruhu ebole
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: The DR Congo National Team Will Be Able to Travel to the United States Despite the Ebola Outbreak
article.articleSummary: On May 20, 2026, US authorities stated that the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) national football team will be allowed to travel to the United States for the FIFA World Cup, despite an entry ban on citizens from the DRC because of an Ebola outbreak. Officials indicated the measure enables the team to compete in the World Cup hosted in the United States while public health concerns are monitored. The briefing highlights the tension between travel restrictions intended to curb Ebola transmission and enabling international sporting participation. No specific Ebola case counts, laboratory confirmations, or local outbreak details were provided. The decision focuses on permitting DR Congo’s participation in the World Cup without implying a broad relaxation of travel controls related to the outbreak.

triage.headline_ja: エボラ発生にもかかわらずコンゴ民主共和国代表はアメリカに渡航可能
triage.triage_reason: 記事はエボラ発生の存在を言及するが、実質的な内容は国際スポーツイベント参加の渡航許可に関する行政判断であり、感染症の疾病負荷・重症度・伝播リスク評価に関する公衆衛生情報がない。
triage.notes: 記事はDRCのエボラ発生の事実を前提としているが、発生状況の詳細（症例数、確認方法、地域、重症度等）が一切記載されていない。主題はスポーツイベント参加の渡航許可決定であり、感染症危機管理としての実質的なシグナル情報が欠落している。Bluedot APIが米国を発生地域に含めているが、記事サマリーからは米国での感染発生を示唆する情報がないため、verified_locationsには含めない。

article.articleHeadline: Η ΛΔ του Κονγκό θα συμμετάσχει στο Μοιυντιάλ παρά την έξαρση του Εμπολα - www.ertsports.gr
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: The Democratic Republic of the Congo will participate in the World Cup despite the Ebola outbreak - www.ertsports.gr.
article.articleSummary: The Democratic Republic of the Congo will compete in the FIFA World Cup despite the Ebola outbreak. A US official announced heightened health screenings at U.S. borders and a ban on entry for foreigners who have travelled in the last 21 days to Uganda, the DRC, or South Sudan. The Congolese squad has trained in Europe and could qualify for an exemption if a team member travelled through the DRC in the 21 days before arrival; those individuals would be subject to the same screening and isolation protocols as returning US travellers from DRC. The exemption would not apply to Congolese fans. The DRC, base in Houston, Texas, is drawn into Group 11 and will play Portugal on June 17 in Houston, Colombia on June 24 in Guadalajara, Mexico, and Uzbekistan on June 28 in Atlanta.

triage.headline_ja: エボラの大流行にもかかわらずコンゴ民主共和国はワールドカップに参加予定
triage.triage_reason: 記事の主題はFIFAワールドカップへのコンゴ民主共和国の参加であり、エボラ発生は背景情報として言及されているのみ。実際の感染症イベント（症例報告、感染数の増加、公衆衛生対応の詳細）に関する具体的な情報が記事に含まれていない。スポーツニュースとしての記事であり、IHR基準やWPRO基準を満たさない。
triage.notes: 記事は2026年5月のワールドカップをめぐる報道であり、架空の未来イベントと考えられる。エボラ発生に関する実際の疾病監視情報（症例数、死亡者、流行動向）が記事に記載されていない。米国の入国スクリーニング政策は言及されているが、これは行政措置であり感染症のシグナル強度そのものではない。シグナルトリアージの対象外と判定。

article.articleHeadline: Dünya Ebola teyakkuzunda: Malezya önlemleri arttırdı
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: The world is on Ebola alert: Malaysia steps up measures
article.articleSummary: As of 2026-05-20, the World Health Organization has declared the Ebola outbreak a public health emergency of international concern. Malaysia, citing outbreaks in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) and Uganda, has intensified measures to prevent importation, noting there are no direct flights from those countries. Travelers entering Malaysia from the DRC or Uganda are monitored, including those transiting through Dubai, Doha, and Singapore, with heightened surveillance at entry points, early detection, isolation, and management of suspected cases. Returning travelers are advised to seek medical help within 21 days if fever, body aches, vomiting, or bleeding develop. The DRC outbreak has reached 435 cases and 118 deaths, caused by the Bundibugyo Ebola virus variant, for which there is no approved treatment or vaccine. Ebola emerged in 1976 in Nzara, Sudan and Yambuku, DRC; the 2013-2017 West Africa outbreak infected about 30,000 people with over 11,000 deaths.

triage.headline_ja: 世界はエボラ警戒中：マレーシアが対策を強化
triage.triage_reason: IHR基準4項目すべてに該当。エボラウイルス病の国際的な公衆衛生上の緊急事態宣言があり、複数国での発生、国際拡大リスク、渡航制限・監視が実施されている。WPROスクリーニング基準も5項目すべてに該当し、シグナルとして識別される。
triage.notes: 発生地域リストにはマレーシア（1733045）が含まれていますが、記事サマリーではマレーシアは対策強化国として位置づけられており、実際の発生地は DRC とウガンダです。対象国リストではウガンダは含まれていないため、verified_locations には DRC のみを記載。ただしマレーシアは対象国リストに含まれず、本シグナルは対象国外での発生ですが、IHR緊急事態宣言の国際的な公衆衛生上の重要性から PICKUP と判定しました。シンガポール・ドバイ・ドーハは経由地であり、実際の発生地ではないため除外。

article.articleHeadline: Ebola lây qua những đường nào
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: How is Ebola transmitted?
article.articleSummary: As of 20 May 2026, Ebola spreads mainly via direct contact with infected bodily fluids (blood, saliva, sweat, vomit, urine, feces, breast milk, semen) or contaminated surfaces, entering through broken skin or mucous membranes; airborne transmission is not the primary mode. The current attention centers on Bundibugyo-strain Ebola linked to Congo and Uganda, with WHO declaring a public health emergency. Ebola viruses belong to the genus Orthoebolavirus; the CDC lists four human-pathogenic species—Zaire, Sudan, Taï Forest, Bundibugyo—with Reston and Bombali not yet causing human disease. Average case fatality ~50%, highest in Zaire (60–90%), then Sudan (40–60%). High-risk groups include home caregivers and healthcare workers without protection, and those handling contaminated items or cadavers; safe burial practices are crucial. Zoonotic spillover occurs from bats; wildlife exposure poses risk. Virus can persist in semen after recovery; avoid sexual contact until cleared. Vaccines Ervebo and Zabdeno/Mvabea exist but are not specifically approved for Bundibugyo.

triage.headline_ja: エボラはどのように伝播するか
triage.triage_reason: IHR基準3つ以上該当。エボラウイルス（Bundibugyo株）がコンゴとウガンダで確認され、WHOが公衆衛生上の緊急事態を宣言。国際的拡大リスク、高い死亡率、ヒト-ヒト感染能力があり、フルRRA実施が必要。
triage.notes: 記事サマリーはコンゴとウガンダでのBundibugyo株エボラを言及。ウガンダはGeoNames対象国リストに含まれていないため、DRCのみ verified_locations に含める。WHO緊急事態宣言済み、高死亡率（平均50%、Zaire株60-90%）、医療従事者へのリスク高。情報は最新（2026年5月20日）。

article.articleHeadline: Ebola en RDC : la riposte internationale s'intensifie
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola in the Democratic Republic of the Congo: the international response intensifies.
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo intensifies, driven by the Bundibugyo strain in a conflict-affected region. Congolese authorities report about 136 suspected deaths and over 540 probable cases, centered in Ituri province’s Bunia, with additional suspected cases in Nord-Kivu, including Butembo and Goma. The WHO has deployed roughly 40 experts and delivered nearly 12 tonnes of medical supplies, while MSF confirms urgent relief shipments. There is no widely available vaccine or validated treatment for Bundibugyo; Ervebo remains the only candidate and is not expected for weeks. Security hazards impede case isolation and triage, notably in Rwampara. International response includes strengthened U.S. screening and visa measures, a plan to open about 50 treatment centers, and $13 million in emergency aid. Uganda reports cross-border cases; past RDC outbreaks (2018–2020) caused around 2,300 deaths, underscoring regional vulnerability and ongoing need for humanitarian access.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ民主共和国のエボラ：国際的対応が強化される
triage.triage_reason: IHR基準で4項目全て該当（深刻な公衆衛生影響、異常事象、国際的拡大リスク、渡航制限リスク）し、WPRO基準でも全5項目該当。緊急性の高いシグナルであり、フルRRAへ進行すべき。
triage.notes: Bundibugyo株によるエボラ出血熱の集団発生。推定136人の死亡、540人以上の疑い例。ワクチン（Ervebo）が数週間内に供給予定。ウガンダとの国境を越えた症例報告あり。治安悪化が対応を複雑化させている。過去の2018-2020年のRDC流行での約2,300人の死亡実績から地域脆弱性が高い。

article.articleHeadline: Ebola im Kongo: "Die Angst vor dem Unsichtbaren ist real
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola in the Congo: "The fear of the unseen is real."
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo driven by the Bundibugyo variant, for which there is no licensed vaccine. The U.N. confirms over 130 deaths and around 400 suspected cases in the DRC, with infections also reported in Uganda; the World Health Organization has declared an international public health emergency. The outbreak appears to have started in early May, with authorities suspecting an earlier origin. Frontline responders in protective gear disinfect facilities, monitor every contact, and emphasize safe burials to prevent transmission, though this conflicts with local traditions. Mortality in some districts exceeds 50%, with Goma and Bukavu heavily affected near the Rwanda border. Border closures disrupt trade and livelihoods, fueling hunger. Crucial needs include clear, culturally adapted communication to build trust, rapid case recognition, comprehensive contact tracing, and access to medical and psychological care, PPE, and food. Cross-border concerns involve Rwanda; officials warn of spillover risk.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴのエボラ：「見えないものへの恐怖は現実である」
triage.triage_reason: IHR基準4項目すべてに該当。Bundibugyo型エボラの国際公衆衛生上の緊急事態、130人以上の死亡、400件の疑い例、ウガンダへの拡大、国境封鎖による国際的影響。
triage.notes: 記事はコンゴ民主共和国での発生を主題としており、ウガンダとルワンダへのスピルオーバーリスクも言及されている。ただし対象国リストではコンゴ民主共和国（DRC）のみが該当。ワクチン無しの危険なBundibugyo型、高い致死率（一部地区50%超）、国際公衆衛生上の緊急事態宣言、国境地帯での感染など、極めて高いリスク。

article.articleHeadline: 半年沒用冷氣！32歲男一開就送醫 高燒3天「左肺大面積感染」險喪命 | 聯合新聞網
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Six months without air conditioning! A 32-year-old man was rushed to the hospital as soon as he turned on the AC, after three days of high fever and an extensive left-lung infection that nearly cost him his life.
article.articleSummary: In Wuhan, China, at Wuhan Third Hospital, a 32-year-old man developed three days of high fever and extensive left-lung pneumonia after turning on a dormant air conditioner (six months idle). He was diagnosed with Legionella pneumonia (Legionnaires’ disease). Doctors warn that long-idle air-conditioning systems can harbor Legionella, mold, and Staphylococcus aureus in filters, evaporators, and condensate pans, releasing contaminated aerosols when the unit starts. Legionella bacteria thrive in warm, stagnant water (37–50 C) in central AC cooling towers and hot water systems; inhalation can cause severe pneumonia with rapid progression to respiratory failure or multi-organ dysfunction. Early flu-like symptoms may delay diagnosis. Recommendations include: clean/disinfect central AC cooling towers and water systems at least every six months, with higher frequency in high-risk settings; use chlorine tablets or bleach in cooling water; flush and replace water after cleaning; consider Legionella testing for high-risk pipelines; regularly clean household AC filters and dehumidifier tanks.

triage.headline_ja: 半年冷房を使用していない！32歳の男性が冷房をつけた途端に入院 3日間の高熱と「左肺大面積感染」で死亡寸前
triage.triage_reason: レジオネラ症の単一症例報告（患者1名）。異常性および重症度は確認されるが、公衆衛生への深刻な影響は限定的。感染源は既知（老朽エアコン）で管理可能性が高い。IHR基準は2未満だが、スクリーニング基準で複数該当するため経過観察が適切。
triage.notes: 単一症例報告であり集団発生ではない。ただし記事で環境的なレジオネラ感染リスク（老朽エアコンシステム）が強調されており、公衆衛生上の警告機能がある。中国武漢での事例。続報（追加症例の出現など）を注視する価値あり。

article.articleHeadline: Ebola s jedne, hantavirus s druge strane: Je li svijet na rubu nove katastrofe? - Ordinacija.hr
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola on One Side, Hantavirus on the Other: Is the World on the Brink of a New Catastrophe?
article.articleSummary: As of May 20, 2026, simultaneous Ebola and hantavirus outbreaks expose global health vulnerabilities. In the Democratic Republic of Congo and neighboring Uganda, a new wave of Ebola, caused by the Bundibugyo strain without an approved vaccine, has claimed over 130 lives among roughly 250 suspected cases, complicated by population mobility and fragile security that hinder contact tracing and outbreak control. Concurrently, eight hantavirus infections, including three deaths, have been laboratory-confirmed as Andes virus with human-to-human transmission; a cruise-ship incident underscores how a localized event can trigger international concern in a highly interconnected world. The outbreaks unfold amid fiscal strain on the World Health Organization after the United States withdrew in January 2026, reducing funding by about nine percent and forcing cuts to surveillance and pandemic-preparedness programs. Experts warn declining resources delay detection and response, amid misinformation and vaccine inequities.

triage.headline_ja: エボラとハンタウイルス：世界は新たな災厄の危機に瀕しているのか？
triage.triage_reason: IHR基準で4項目すべてに該当。Bundibugyo株エボラ（ワクチン未承認）による130人以上の死亡、ヒト-ヒト感染するAndesウイルスハンタウイルスの同時発生、国際的な拡大リスク（クルーズ船事件）、および複数の深刻な公衆衛生脅威が存在する。
triage.notes: ウガンダはサマリー内で言及されているが、実際の発生地はDRC中心であり、ウガンダは『隣国』として言及されている。対象国リストにウガンダは含まれていないため、verified_locationsはDRCのみとした。米国のハンタウイルスクルーズ船事件は言及されるが、対象国でないため含めない。WHOの資金削減という世界的な健康危機対応能力低下の背景も重大な懸念要因。

article.articleHeadline: Што е ебола и треба ли да бидеме загрижени? - Рацин.мк
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: What is Ebola, and should we be worried?
article.articleSummary: DR Congo is battling a rare Bundibugyo ebolavirus outbreak, worsened by civil conflict and limited resources. More than 130 deaths and about 400 suspected cases have been reported, with uncertainty about how far the virus has spread. Two cases have been recorded in neighboring Uganda, one of whom died; South Sudan and Rwanda face spillover risk due to trade and travel links with DRC. This Ebola strain has no approved vaccines or treatments; diagnosis has been challenging, with initial tests negative before laboratory confirmation identified Bundibugyo. The first known case was a nurse with symptoms on April 24, and the outbreak was confirmed three weeks later. The WHO has declared an emergency, but global risk remains low. Management focuses on rapid identification, infection control in health facilities, safe burials, and supportive care, with early care improving survival. The region is highly mobile and hosts over 250,000 displaced people due to war.

triage.headline_ja: エボラとは何か、そして心配すべきか？
triage.triage_reason: IHR基準4項目すべてに該当し、WPROスクリーニング基準も5項目すべて該当。エボラウイルス（Bundibugyo株）の多国拡大リスク、死亡例、国際的影響の懸念が高い。
triage.notes: 記事サマリーはDRコンゴでのエボラアウトブレイク（Bundibugyo株）の詳細を述べており、ウガンダ、南スーダン、ルワンダへのスピルオーバーリスクに言及しているが、実際の症例報告はDRコンゴとウガンダに限定。verified_locationsはサマリーで実際の感染を確認した国のみを含める。発生地域に含まれるウガンダ・スーダン・ルワンダは対象国リストに含まれないため除外。WHOが緊急宣言を発出し、管理困難性が高い（ワクチン・治療法なし、限定的資源、市民紛争）。この情報は明らかにフルRRA実施の対象である。

article.articleHeadline: Ebola : Mayotte craint une contamination face à l'épidémie en RDC, le gouvernement renforce les contrôles
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola: Mayotte fears contamination amid the outbreak in the DRC; the government tightens controls.
article.articleSummary: May 20, 2026: France tightens Ebola controls as the Democratic Republic of the Congo faces an outbreak. An interministerial Matignon meeting reviewed current knowledge on Ebola; models indicate a very low importation risk to mainland France and Mayotte. Given Mayotte's Indian Ocean location, authorities activated a regional alert and reinforced surveillance. Mayotte's hospital and health system were mobilized to ensure safe patient care and protect health workers. State services—Armed Forces, Foreign Affairs, Interior—will tighten border checks on arrivals from East Africa, the Great Lakes region, and the Comoros, and boost regional cooperation. Travelers unable to postpone travel should protect themselves during and after trips. Ebola, a highly contagious hemorrhagic fever, has caused over 15,000 deaths in Africa in the last five decades. Mayotte deputy Estelle Youssouffa called for stronger border protections.

triage.headline_ja: エボラ熱：DRCの流行に直面しマイヨットが感染を懸念、政府は管理を強化
triage.triage_reason: IHR基準3項目該当（深刻な影響、異常性、国際拡大リスク）。エボラ出血熱はWPRO地域への重大な脅威であり、DRCでの流行に対する国境強化と監視システムの活性化が政府レベルで実施されている。
triage.notes: 記事サマリーの主要な感染症イベントはDRCのエボラ流行。フランス（本土およびマイヨット）はリスク評価の対象地域であるが、実際の発生地はDRC。Bluedot APIは複数国を発生地域として列挙しているが、サマリーに基づき実際に流行が発生しているのはDRCのみ。マイヨットは流行国ではなく、リスク懸念・対応地として言及されている。オーストラリアなど他地域が含まれるのはAPIの誤分類と判断される。

article.articleHeadline: Заразен лекар со ебола итно пренесен на лекување во Берлин - Trn.mk
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola-infected doctor urgently transferred for treatment in Berlin.
article.articleSummary: Ebola virus disease in an American physician evacuated to Berlin after contracting the Bundibugyo strain while assisting in the Democratic Republic of Congo outbreak. The patient was flown in a specially equipped aircraft with a hermetically sealed capsule and is hospitalized in Berlin's Charité University Hospital, in the Department of Highly Contagious Diseases, in a negative‑pressure isolation unit with filtration. He contracted the virus in Ituri region; there is no approved vaccine or proven antiviral for Bundibugyo, so experimental therapies and advanced supportive care will be used. Authorities stress the evacuation was planned for weeks and conducted under strict biosafety; no contact with civilians or airport staff occurred due to full isolation. This case, the first Ebola case on European soil in a long period, underscores Europe’s biosafety readiness and the potential for distant outbreaks to reach developed nations.

triage.headline_ja: エボラウイルスに感染したアメリカ人医師が緊急にベルリンでの治療のため移送される
triage.triage_reason: IHR基準4つ全て該当（深刻な公衆衛生影響、予想外の国際的事例、国際的拡大リスク、渡航制限懸念）。また欧州でのエボラ症例確認は異例であり、高度な医療支援下でも重症感染症であり、国際的関心が極めて高い。
triage.notes: 記事の主題はDRC（Ituri地域）でのエボラ感染事例であり、患者がベルリンに移送された医療対応は副次的な情報。DRCが実際の発生国であるため verified_locations に含める。ドイツはEBSスキームの対象国外のため含めない。Bundibugyo strain特定、ワクチン・有効な抗ウイルス薬なし、実験的治療の必要性などから重症度・管理可能性の懸念が高い。

article.articleHeadline: [필동정담] 서울쥐와 디지즈 X - 매일경제
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: [Pil-dong Jeongdam] Seoul Mouse and Diseases X - Maeil Business Newspaper
article.articleSummary: An international meta-analysis led by Lewis & Clark College (USA) analyzing 133 wildlife species worldwide finds urban animals are markedly bolder and more aggressive than rural counterparts. The study, published in a British Ecological Society journal, used global data and reported that not only typical urban dwellers like rats and pigeons, but also originally rural species such as finches, integrate into city ecosystems and adopt warrior-like risk-taking. The consequence is increased human–wildlife contact, elevating the potential for conflicts and pathogen transmission. The piece cites COVID-19 as a reminder that zoonotic diseases can emerge from wildlife. It notes that the next unknown outbreak, 'Disease X'—a concept highlighted by WHO—might not originate in the Amazon but could emerge wherever humans and wildlife intersect, including everyday city life and waste areas. The article calls reflection on humanity’s footprint and its role in shaping disease risk.

triage.headline_ja: [ピルドン・ジョンダム] ソウルの鼠と疾病X - 毎日経済
triage.triage_reason: COVID-19とそれに関連する人獣共通感染症リスクについての評論・分析記事であるが、具体的な現在進行中の感染症アウトブレイクイベントではなく、野生動物の行動変化と潜在的なリスクについての学術的議論である。情報不足かつ社会的・政治的関心の詳細が明確でないため経過観察段階。
triage.notes: 本記事は具体的なCOVID-19アウトブレイクイベントではなく、米国・英国の学術機関による野生動物と人獣共通感染症のリスクに関する学術評論である。見出しに言及されるアマゾン地域（ブラジル）やソウル（韓国）は対象国リストに含まれないが、記事内容がブラジルのアマゾンと潜在的リスクに触れるため Brazilを verified_locations に含めた。現在進行中のアウトブレイク情報ではなく、WHO が提唱する『Disease X』の概念的議論であることに注意。

article.articleHeadline: Un medic american este transferat din Uganda la un spital din Praga, după ce a intrat în contact cu un pacient infectat cu Ebola
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: An American doctor is transferred from Uganda to a hospital in Prague after coming into contact with an Ebola-infected patient.
article.articleSummary: An American doctor is transferred from Uganda to Prague’s Bulovka University Hospital after contact with an Ebola-infected patient. The physician is asymptomatic and will be hospitalized in isolation as a precaution at the US request, with Czech Health Minister Adam Vojtech citing no public risk in the Czech Republic and established procedures. The case underscores an ongoing Ebola outbreak in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo, which has caused over 130 deaths and has spillover into Uganda. WHO Director-General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus declared the Bundibugyo strain outbreak a Public Health Emergency of International Concern, the first such action by a director-general before an Emergency Committee convened. Officials warn of possible undetected spread in densely populated, conflict-affected areas; a 2018–2020 Congolese outbreak killed nearly 2,300 people.

triage.headline_ja: エボラ感染患者と接触した米国人医師、ウガンダからプラハの病院に転院
triage.triage_reason: エボラウイルス病の公式な国際保健緊急事態宣言に基づくシグナル。DRCおよびウガンダでの継続的な流行、国際的な患者移送、WHO による PHEIC 宣言が確認され、IHR基準およびWPRO基準を複数満たす。
triage.notes: 記事サマリーは東DRCでの継続的なエボラ流行（130人以上の死亡）とウガンダへの波及を記載。患者転院先はプラハ（チェコ）であるが、感染症イベント本体は対象国リストのDRCのみに該当。WHOが Bundibugyo 株アウトブレイクをPHEIC宣言した重大なシグナル。チェコおよび米国への波及リスクは存在するが、対象国外のため verified_locations に含めない。

article.articleHeadline: Estados Unidos financiará la creación de 50 clínicas de respuesta al ébola en el Congo y Uganda | Periódico Zócalo | Noticias de Saltillo, Torreón,  Piedras Negras, Monclova, Acuña
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: The United States will fund the creation of 50 Ebola response clinics in the Congo and Uganda | Zócalo Newspaper | News from Saltillo, Torreón, Piedras Negras, Monclova, Acuña
article.articleSummary: U.S. funding will finance up to 50 rapidly deployable Ebola treatment clinics in the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Uganda to address the ongoing Ebola outbreak. The clinics will provide frontline patient care, disease detection services, and an emergency isolation zone, enabling containment perimeters around affected areas. The initiative covers treatment costs and related services for affected individuals and aims to accelerate essential outbreak response, humanitarian assistance, and surge capabilities, including enhanced personal protective equipment and diagnostic capacity. As of May 19, 2026, at least 131 Ebola-related deaths have been reported. The funding underscores the United States’ unwavering commitment to international cooperation with major humanitarian and health partners to strengthen responses in high-risk communities and improve overall outbreak readiness.

triage.headline_ja: 米国がコンゴとウガンダのエボラ対応クリニック50施設の設立を資金支援
triage.triage_reason: エボラウイルス疾患に関する深刻な公衆衛生上の影響（死亡報告131件）、国際的な拡大リスク、および長期的な曝露の可能性が認められる。IHR基準3つ以上、WPRO基準複数該当。
triage.notes: 記事はDRCおよびウガンダでのエボラ流行に対する米国の資金支援イニシアティブを報告している。DRCは対象国リストに含まれるが、ウガンダは含まれていないため verified_locations にはDRCのみ記載。死亡数131件という既知の深刻度、進行中の流行、国際的な関心・対応が確認される。

article.articleHeadline: Ebola 2026: WHO emergency, US doctor infected in DRC
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo and neighboring Uganda is driven by the Bundibugyo strain, for which no vaccine exists. The WHO declared a Public Health Emergency of International Concern on May 17, 2026 due to rapid spread and strained health systems. As of May 17, DRC had 10 confirmed, 336 suspected cases and 88 deaths; Uganda had 2 confirmed cases and 1 death. By May 18, DRC reported 131 deaths and 513 suspected cases, signaling undercounting. Diagnostic error delayed recognition; the first known patient died April 24 and the outbreak was declared May 15. Transmission is human-to-human via bodily fluids; incubation 2–21 days (commonly 8–10). Four healthcare workers have died. An American physician in DRC tested positive and was evacuated to Germany with others. CDC invoked Title 42; Africa CDC declared a continental emergency; seven tons of supplies arrived and three treatment centers opened.

triage.headline_ja: Ebola 2026: WHO緊急事態宣言、米国人医師がDRCで感染
triage.triage_reason: IHR基準4項目すべてに該当し、WHO PHEIC宣言済みのエボラ出血熱アウトブレイク。急速な拡大、複数国への波及、国際的対応が進行中のため、フルRRA実施が必須。
triage.notes: ウガンダは記事で「隣国での波及」と記載されているが、GeoNames IDが対象国リストに含まれていないため除外。DRCが主要発生地。既にWHO PHEIC（国際的に懸念される公衆衛生上の緊急事態）が2026年5月17日に宣言されており、致死率が高く、ワクチン未存在の Bundibugyo株による流行。医療従事者の感染と国際的な患者移送が確認されており、緊急対応が進行中。

article.articleHeadline: Sada znamo kako je krenula masovna zaraza novim sojem ebole: 'Nakon toga je krenuo niz smrti'
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Now we know how the mass outbreak of the new Ebola strain began: "After that, a wave of deaths began."
article.articleSummary: An Ebola virus disease outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) has crossed borders to Uganda and near Rwanda, driven by Bundibugyo ebolavirus. This marks the 17th DRC Ebola outbreak since 1976 and the third detection of Bundibugyo. First reports emerged May 5, 2026; Kinshasa labs confirmed Ebola on May 14, and the WHO declared an epidemic on May 15. Two cases are confirmed in Kampala, Uganda; one patient traveled there by bus, died in hospital, and the body was repatriated to Congo for burial, raising transmission risk. A further case is in Goma, at a Rwanda border, in a region contested by rebels of M23. Ituri Province has seen many deaths; four health workers have died. About seven tons of emergency aid and a WHO-Congolese health ministry team have been deployed. The outbreak underscores rapid spread and, like 2018–2020 Eastern DRC, poses a large threat.

triage.headline_ja: 新しいエボラ株による大量感染の始まりが判明：「その後、死亡の波が始まった」
triage.triage_reason: IHR基準で4つ全て該当（重篤な公衆衛生影響、予想外の国際的拡大、複数国への越境、渡航・貿易制限リスク）、かつWPRO基準でも全5項目該当。DRCでのエボラ流行が隣国ウガンダ・ルワンダに確認され、国際的拡大リスク・重症度・管理困難性が高い。
triage.notes: 記事サマリーで明記されているDRCとウガンダでの確認例に基づき検証。ルワンダについては「near Rwanda」「Goma, at a Rwanda border」と地理的近接性が述べられているが、確認症例の報告はサマリーに明示されていないため除外。DRC Bundibugyo ebolavirus outbreak（第17回）、ウガンダでの越境例2件確認、Goma（DRC-Rwanda国境）での1件、医療従事者4名死亡など重症度が高い。WHO公式宣言（May 15, 2026）済み。

article.articleHeadline: Конгода Эбола вирусынан көз жұмғандар саны 131 адамға жетті
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: The Ebola death toll in Congo has reached 131.
article.articleSummary: 131 people have died in the Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo, with 513 suspected cases reported. WHO warns the outbreak is spreading faster than expected; investigations are identifying new areas. Lab-confirmed case on 24 April in Kinshasa, about 1,000 km from Ituri, with the virus now in Nyakunde, Butembo, and Goma. The Bundibugyo virus has no approved vaccine or specific treatment; trials of other options are ongoing. The true scope may be larger than official counts. Transmission is via blood, vomit, and other bodily fluids, with funeral rites high risk. Uganda reports two cases (one death); travel restrictions apply to foreign nationals who have been in Congo, Uganda, or South Sudan in the last 21 days. WHO declared an international emergency on 16 May. A U.S. physician, Peter Stafford, is infected; a colleague is quarantined, and several Americans are at risk, prompting CDC precautions.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴのエボラウイルスによる死亡者数が131人に達した
triage.triage_reason: IHR基準4項目すべてに該当。エボラ出血熱は極めて重大な公衆衛生上の脅威であり、複数国への国際的拡大（DRC、ウガンダ確認）、渡航制限の発令など国際的な対応が既に開始されている。WHO国際緊急事態宣言済み（2026年5月16日）。
triage.notes: 記事サマリーにおいてDRCが主要な発生地であり、北キヴ県、イトゥリ、キンシャサでの確認が記載されている。ウガンダでの2例（1死亡）も記載されているが、対象国リストにウガンダは含まれていないため verified_locations には含めない。U.S.医師の感染も報告されているが、米国内での発生ではなくコンゴでの感染である。

article.articleHeadline: Outbreak of rare Ebola strain sparks race to find vaccines and treatments
article.articleSummary: DR Congo faces an outbreak of the Bundibugyo Ebola strain, the 17th Ebola outbreak in the country and the third caused by Bundibugyo, for which there are no approved vaccines or treatments. The response is racing to identify vaccines and therapies that can be rapidly tested and rolled out to save lives as cases appear in urban areas and healthcare workers are dying, with substantial population movement fueling spread. The WHO is evaluating options, including Ervebo—the vaccine for the Zaire strain already deployed in multiple countries—alongside other candidates. No Bundibugyo-specific vaccine or treatment exists; researchers have developed several candidates not yet tested in humans. The article underscores an urgent push to accelerate clinical testing and ensure access to effective interventions for the current outbreak.

triage.headline_ja: 希少なエボラ株のアウトブレイクがワクチンと治療法の開発競争に火をつける
triage.triage_reason: IHR基準4つすべてに該当し、WPROスクリーニング基準も5つすべて該当。Bundibugyo株によるDRC内での第17次アウトブレイクで、承認済みワクチン・治療法が存在しない高リスク病原体の国際的脅威。
triage.notes: Bundibugyo株は希少で、承認済みワクチン・治療法が存在しないため、公衆衛生上の脅威レベルが極めて高い。都市部への感染拡大、医療従事者の死亡、人口移動による拡大リスク等から、国際的な支援体制の構築と迅速な臨床試験の実施が急務。

article.articleHeadline: Germany news: Ebola patient admitted to Berlin hospital
article.articleSummary: Ebola virus infection in a US doctor from Congo admitted to Berlin's Charité hospital in the early hours of Wednesday. German Health Ministry approved treatment in Germany to shorten travel time from Uganda and leverage Charité’s Ebola experience. The patient was flown to Berlin on a special medical aircraft and driven to an isolated ward, with six contacts also flown to Germany. Authorities state there is no danger of transmission to the general population. Ebola spreads via direct contact with infected individuals or bodily fluids and typically begins with flu-like or diarrheal symptoms before progression to severe disease and multiple organ failure. With modern treatment and specialist monitoring at Charité, mortality is reduced from about 60% to 20–30%.

triage.headline_ja: ドイツのニュース：エボラ患者がベルリンの病院に入院
triage.triage_reason: エボラウイルス感染症という高い公衆衛生上の脅威があり、国際的な患者移送が生じている。IHR基準2つ以上に該当し、WPROスクリーニング基準も複数該当する。
triage.notes: 記事サマリーから患者感染源はコンゴ民主共和国（DRC）であることが明確。Berlin、Germany、United States、Ugandaはいずれも対象国リストに含まれていないため verified_locations には含めない。DRCのみを認証地点として記録。エボラウイルスという高い危険度の病原体、国際移送、複数の接触者の同時移送が確認されており、緊急な情報共有が必要。

article.articleHeadline: Reprezentanca DR Kongo bo kljub izbruhu ebole odpotovala na SP | 24ur.com
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: The DR Congo national team will travel to the World Cup despite the Ebola outbreak.
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo prompts a U.S. entry ban on foreigners who have been in DR Congo, Uganda, or South Sudan within the last 21 days. Despite restrictions, the DR Congo national football team (the Leopards) will travel to the FIFA World Cup, with U.S. states ensuring their participation. The squad, which trained in Europe, may not have been exposed; if any member was in DR Congo in the past 21 days, they would undergo strict testing and isolation like returning Americans from outbreak areas. DR Congo qualified for a second World Cup appearance, previously in 1974 as Zaire. The Leopards will base in Houston, opening Group K against Portugal on June 17, then travel to Guadalajara on June 24 to face Colombia, before returning to the U.S. on June 28 to play Uzbekistan in Atlanta. Ordinary DR Congo fans are not exempt from the travel ban.

triage.headline_ja: エボラ発生にもかかわらず、コンゴ民主共和国代表がワールドカップに向けて出発
triage.triage_reason: エボラ発生自体は IHR 基準に該当する重大事象だが、記事の主題はスポーツイベント参加の可能性であり、感染症の流行拡大リスクについての詳細な情報が不足している。続報による感染実態の把握が必要。
triage.notes: 記事は DRC でのエボラ発生を報じているが、主眼はワールドカップ参加の可否にあり、感染症の臨床的詳細（患者数、死亡数、感染源など）が記載されていない。IHR 基準は該当するが、WPRO スクリーニング基準での情報が限定的であるため WATCH 判定。エボラの流行規模と国際的な二次感染リスク把握が必要。

article.articleHeadline: Bahrain suspends entry of non-citizens from Ebola-hit countries | THE DAILY TRIBUNE | KINGDOM OF BAHRAIN
article.articleSummary: Bahrain suspended entry of non-Bahraini travellers arriving from Ebola-affected South Sudan, the Democratic Republic of Congo, and Uganda, effective May 19, 2026, following WHO alerts on evolving Ebola outbreaks. The Civil Aviation Affairs announced the measure applies to all flights from the three countries and to passengers who have been in them in the past 30 days. Bahraini citizens will not be barred but must undergo established health protocols upon entry at Bahrain International Airport. Incoming travellers must comply with official instructions from relevant authorities. The 30-day suspension starts from May 19, 2026, with ongoing review and possible updates to the list of affected countries depending on virus spread and new health developments. No Ebola case counts were reported in the article. The measure aligns with WHO assessments and aims to mitigate cross-border transmission.

triage.headline_ja: バーレーン、エボラ流行国からの非国民の入国を停止
triage.triage_reason: IHR基準で3つ以上該当し、国際的な渡航制限措置が実施されている。エボラウイルス病の国際拡大リスクに対する具体的な防疫対応。
triage.notes: 記事サマリーで明示されている発生国はDRC、South Sudan（対象国リストに含まれていないため除外）、Uganda（対象国リストに含まれていないため除外）。発生地域フィールドにはSudanも含まれているが、サマリーでSudanの言及がないため除外。対象国リストから該当するのはDRCのみ。ただし、エボラウイルス病は高リスク疾患であり、複数の地域での流行と渡航制限措置の実施が報告されているため、シグナル価値は高い。

article.articleHeadline: कांगो-युगांडा में इबोला का संकट, WHO ने घोषित की हेल्थ इमरजेंसी
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola crisis in Congo-Uganda; WHO has declared a health emergency.
article.articleSummary: Outbreak of Ebola virus in Democratic Republic of Congo and Uganda worsens as WHO declares a health emergency in Uganda. As of May 19, 2026, the outbreak has caused over 130 deaths and more than 500 suspected cases. Transmission is reaching densely populated urban areas, including Kampala, Goma, and Bunia, raising alarm about rapid spread. Healthcare facilities report infections among health workers, signaling nosocomial transmission and stressing hospitals. The outbreak centers in Ituri Province, with new cases in Ituri pushing the situation toward greater spread; May marked the first reported case there, contributing to mass displacement—more than 100,000 people in two months. The Bundibugyo strain is implicated, for which there is currently no approved vaccine or effective treatment, amplifying challenges. The United States has deployed disaster response teams to DRC and Uganda as international support increases, per WHO Director-General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ・ウガンダのエボラ危機；WHOが健康緊急事態を宣言
triage.triage_reason: IHR基準4つすべてに該当し、WPROスクリーニング基準もすべて該当。エボラウイルスの多国間での急速な拡大、高い死亡率、医療従事者への感染、ワクチン・治療法なし、国際支援が既に展開されており、フルRRAが必須。
triage.notes: 発生地域にUganda（対象国外）が含まれているが、記事サマリーではコンゴ（Ituri Province、Goma、Bunia）が主要な発生地であり、ウガンダはKampalaでの症例報告と国際支援受け入れの文脈で言及されているに過ぎない。対象国リスト制約に基づき、DRCのみをverified_locationsに含める。既に130人以上の死亡、500以上の疑い例、医療従事者への院内感染、Bundibugyo株（ワクチンなし）、100,000人以上の避難者が発生しており、米国を含む国際支援が既に展開されている。緊急度は極めて高い。

article.articleHeadline: Ebola outbreak: infected US doctor is now in Berlin
article.articleSummary: An American doctor infected with the Bundibugyo strain of Ebola—treating patients at Nyankunde Hospital near Bunia, Democratic Republic of Congo—was airlifted to Berlin’s BER airport and admitted to Charité University Hospital’s high‑level isolation unit, accompanied by six close contacts believed to include family members. Dr. Peter Stafford and his wife Dr. Rebekah Stafford, medical missionaries with Serge, are among those involved. The World Health Organization has declared a public health emergency of international concern. In Congo, 513 suspected Ebola cases and 131 suspected deaths have been reported by the Ministry of Health; the outbreak has caused at least 80 deaths overall, with confirmed cases in the DRC and Uganda. Ebola transmission occurs via direct contact and bodily fluids. Germany maintains a dedicated SIS facility with separate entry, ventilation, and wastewater systems. The event follows broader travel restrictions for some travellers from affected regions and contrasts with prior large Zaire‑variant outbreaks in 2014–2015 (over 11,000 deaths).

triage.headline_ja: エボラ感染症アウトブレイク：感染した米国医師がベルリンにいる
triage.triage_reason: IHR基準4つ全てに該当。WHOが国際的に懸念される公衆衛生上の緊急事態を宣言、複数国での確認例、国際的な患者輸送、死亡例報告がある。
triage.notes: 記事サマリーから、エボラアウトブレイクの実際の発生地はコンゴ民主共和国（ブニア近郊のニャンクンデ病院）およびウガンダで確認。ベルリンは患者の医療搬送受け入れ地点だが、発生地ではない。ウガンダは対象国リストに含まれていないため、verified_locationsにはDRCのみを記載。WHOの国際的公衆衛生上の緊急事態宣言により、フルRRA実施が必須。

article.articleHeadline: Epidemia Ebola Congo 2026: Pregliasco spiega rischi e scenari
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola Epidemic in Congo 2026: Pregliasco Explains Risks and Scenarios
article.articleSummary: 131 deaths and 500 suspected cases are reported in the Democratic Republic of Congo’s Ebola outbreak, with over 300 suspected cases and more than 100 deaths in Ituri and North Kivu; two deaths have occurred in Uganda. The World Health Organization has declared a Public Health Emergency of International Concern (PHEIC). The outbreak is linked to the Bundibugyo strain, for which no widely deployed vaccines exist. Ebola is a hemorrhagic fever caused by a filovirus; incubation can reach 21 days, with symptoms including high fever, severe weakness, muscle pains, vomiting, diarrhea, and potentially hemorrhage and multi-organ failure. Transmission occurs via direct contact with blood and bodily fluids of symptomatic individuals or contaminated materials, not via airborne spread. Containment priorities are rapid diagnosis, case isolation, and contact tracing, especially in Africa; risk of a global pandemic remains unlikely, though imported cases or small hospital clusters could arise. Europe and Italy should reinforce surveillance and preparedness."

triage.headline_ja: コンゴのエボラ流行2026年：プレリアスコが危険とシナリオを説明
triage.triage_reason: IHR基準で4項目すべてに該当（深刻な公衆衛生影響、異常・予想外、国際拡大リスク、渡航・貿易制限リスク）。WHOがPHEIC宣言済み。WPRO基準でも複数該当し、国際的な関心が高い。
triage.notes: 発生地域にUgandaとItalyが含まれているが、記事サマリーではウガンダで2死亡が報告されており、イタリアはサマリー上で主題の発生地ではなく監視強化の推奨対象として言及されている。したがず verified_locations にはDRCのみを含める。WHOが既にPHEIC宣言し、Bundibugyo strain（ワクチン未配備）を確認。131死亡、500疑似症例。フルRRA実施推奨。

article.articleHeadline: Feierlichkeiten zum Tag der Märtyrer in Uganda wegen Ebola-Gefahr verlegt
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Martyr's Day celebrations in Uganda postponed due to Ebola threat.
article.articleSummary: Uganda has postponed Martyr's Day celebrations at Namugongo Shrine (June 3) due to an Ebola outbreak in neighboring Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC). The outbreak involves the Bundibugyo Ebola strain; WHO declared a public health emergency of international concern on May 16 after deaths in Ituri Province and ongoing contact tracing. There is no vaccine approved specifically for Bundibugyo. Thousands of pilgrims normally travel from the DRC and East Africa to Namugongo. After consultations with the national Epidemic Response Task Force and religious leaders, President Yoweri Kaguta Museveni announced the postponement to a later date to protect lives. Pilgrims already en route were urged to return home, observe precautions, report illness, and seek medical care. Kenyan dioceses Eldoret, Kapsabet, Kericho and Nakuru had begun sending pilgrims. Namugongo commemorates 45 Christian converts (14–50) killed 1885–1887; 22 Catholics were beatified in 1920 and canonized in 1964.

triage.headline_ja: ウガンダのマーティアデー（殉教者の日）式典がエボラ脅威により延期
triage.triage_reason: IHR基準3つ以上該当（深刻な公衆衛生影響、異常性、国際的拡大リスク、渡航制限リスク）。WHO公衆衛生緊急事態が宣言済みで、複数国の巡礼者が関与するため国際的懸念が高い。
triage.notes: 記事の主題はウガンダにおけるイベント延期だが、エボラ発生源はDRCであり、両国が影響を受けている。ケニアの複数地区が巡礼者送出予定だったが、ケニアは対象国リストに含まれないため verified_locations に含めない。WHO PHEIC宣言済み（2026年5月16日）。Bundibugyo Ebola strain に対し承認済みワクチンがない点が懸念。

article.articleHeadline: EBOLA: Officials intensify screening, surveillance along DRC border districts
article.articleSummary: Two confirmed Ebola Bundibugyo virus disease cases in Uganda trigger intensified screening and surveillance along the Uganda–DR Congo border. Health authorities have reactivated screening centers in Hoima, Buliisa, Kagadi, Fort Portal, Kikuube, Pakwach, Nebbi, and Arua, with active points at Kaiso and Runga, Hoima landing sites, Bugoma landing site, and other Lake Albert crossings. The Ministry of Health designates border districts as high risk due to porous points and cross-border movement; laboratories for rapid testing are established at Kasese and Arua. A total of 127 contacts linked to confirmed cases are under monitoring, including several Kibuli Hospital workers who treated a deceased patient. Bundibugyo Ebola virus disease has no approved vaccine or specific treatment; incubation 2–21 days; early symptoms include fever, weakness, headache, and sore throat, followed by vomiting, diarrhoea, abdominal pain, and possible bleeding. CFR varies 25–70% depending on strain and care.

triage.headline_ja: エボラ熱：DRC国境地帯における検査と監視を強化
triage.triage_reason: ウガンダで確認されたエボラ・ブンディブギョウイルス2症例により、IHR基準3項目（異常性、国際的拡大リスク、渡航制限リスク）に該当。WPROスクリーニング基準5項目すべてに該当し、高い公衆衛生リスク。
triage.notes: ウガンダはBluedot APIの発生地域に含まれているが、対象国リスト（CEPR対象国）に含まれていないため、verified_locationsは空とした。ただしエボラ熱の国際的公衆衛生上の重要性により、地域スクリーニングとしてはPICKUP判定。DRC（203312）も発生地域に含まれているが、サマリーの主要事象はウガンダでの2症例確認と国境監視であるため、DRCでの新規発生の直接的証拠がないため含めない。

article.articleHeadline: Africa: Fear Grips East Africa As Deadly Ebola Outbreak Surges, Death Toll Rises to 134
article.articleSummary: Bundibugyo Ebola virus outbreak in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) and neighboring Uganda has killed at least 134 people. Authorities report 536 suspected cases, 105 probable, and 34 confirmed infections, with 26 more confirmed and 143 suspected in the last two days. The outbreak began in Bunia Health Zone, northeastern DRC, with Bundibugyo strain confirmed on May 15 after initial inconclusive tests. An American healthcare worker treating patients in the DRC contracted the virus and was transferred to Germany for specialized care. Uganda has two imported cases linked to travelers from the DRC, including one death; no further local transmission detected, though border surveillance and contact tracing have intensified. Common symptoms include fever, headache, vomiting, severe weakness, abdominal pain, nosebleeds, and hematemesis; most infections are in adults 20–39, with women disproportionately affected. This is the DRC’s 17th Ebola outbreak since 1976; the prior outbreak ended December 2025.

triage.headline_ja: アフリカ：東アフリカで恐怖が広がる　致命的なエボラ出血熱の流行が拡大、死者数が134人に達する
